raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

The Muse Glimmer and Muse Spark (NaViT) vision encoders read window layouts back from the GPU, once per image or frame group. Under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, which the CI test image sets (#43107), every Glimmer image or video request raises. The check is off by default, so users don't see the error, but the syncs still run on every request.

This PR builds those layouts on the host. For Glimmer, it also runs the vision prep once per call instead of once per group.

## Claims

- No GPU<->CPU syncs in either encoder: Glimmer 879 → 0 and NaViT 817 → 0 over 126 encoder calls.
- Glimmer encodes 32-frame video 1.15–1.22× faster, depending on the benchmark (see below).
- No change for images or serving. VisionArena p99 TTFT is 509 ms vs 507 / 506 ms on main, over 1,000 requests.
- Outputs are bit-identical to main on all 126 calls, with real Glimmer vision weights and random pixel values, on H100 (FlashAttention 3) and L4 (FlashAttention 2).
- Peak GPU memory is never above main (worst ratio 0.998), so the encoder profiling budget does not grow.

## Validation

**Tests** (`pytest -v tests/models/multimodal/test_muse_vision_encoders.py`, L4):

```text
# main (the other 28 failures call helpers or signatures added by this PR)
FAILED ...::test_glimmer_engine_has_no_gpu_sync
FAILED ...::test_glimmer_vision_encoder_has_no_gpu_sync
FAILED ...::test_navit_has_no_gpu_sync
vllm/model_executor/models/muse_glimmer.py:697: in _get_sparse_permutation
E   RuntimeError: GPU<->CPU sync detected - avoid it or wrap with gpu_sync_allowed()
31 failed, 5 passed

# this PR
36 passed

# earlier revision of this PR, one patch-projection matmul per call
E   AssertionError: assert [92] == [60, 16, 16]
FAILED ...::test_glimmer_vision_encoder_projects_patches_per_group
1 failed, 35 passed
```

The engine test sends an image and a video request through `vllm_runner` with dummy weights. These tests have not yet run on the H200 CI lane.

**Encoder, main vs this PR.** Same process, real `meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B` vision weights, H100, bf16. VisionArena image sizes through Glimmer's processor, plus video and bursts. 3 rounds, shuffled call order, rotated arm order. Each row sums the per-call medians.

| calls | n | main ms | PR ms | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| one image | 40 | 1222.0 | 1222.0 | 1.000× |
| 2–4 images | 45 | 3378.5 | 3342.6 | 1.011× |
| Poisson-sized | 20 | 703.0 | 701.4 | 1.002× |
| size extremes, up to 4096 tokens | 10 | 765.7 | 766.7 | 0.999× |
| video, 8 / 32 / 96 frames | 3 | 401.5 | 358.3 | 1.121× |
| bursts, 8k / 16k tokens | 8 | 3694.7 | 3619.6 | 1.021× |
| total | 126 | 10165.4 | 10010.7 | 1.015× |

Noise is about 1 %, so I read the image rows as unchanged. Prep launches drop from 94 to 20 for one image and from 1,490 to 37 for 32-frame video.

**`vllm bench mm-processor`, 32-frame 720p video.** Encoder forward is 87.5 ms vs 106.2 / 107.8 ms on main (1.22×). The harness above gives 83.0 vs 95.1 ms (1.15×) for the same frame count. The two differ in host and input, and I did not isolate how much each contributes.

**`vllm bench serve`.** `RedHatAI/Muse-Glimmer-30B-FP8-block` (vision tower BF16), H100, main → PR → main on one host, 0 failed requests.

| workload | concurrency | requests | req/s, main | PR | median TTFT ms, main | PR | p99 TTFT ms, main | PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| VisionArena, 8 output tokens | 1 | 1,000 | 3.52 / 3.51 | 3.53 | 156 / 159 | 157 | 507 / 506 | 509 |
| 32-frame 720p video | 1 | 30 | 0.65 / 0.68 | 0.67 | 613 / 589 | 571 | 826 / 669 | 791 |
| 4 images per request | 16 | 200 | 1.25 / 1.26 | 1.31 | 6939 / 7111 | 5527 | 14744 / 14284 | 13668 |

I'm not claiming a serving gain. The 4-image gap is far larger than the roughly 1 % encoder change can explain, and an earlier run of the same workload had main alone at 6209 / 5156 ms. The video rows have only 30 requests.

<details><summary>Reproduction</summary>

```bash
vllm serve RedHatAI/Muse-Glimmer-30B-FP8-block --port 8000 --max-model-len 16384 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --seed 0 --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 4, "video": 1}'

# VisionArena
vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --model RedHatAI/Muse-Glimmer-30B-FP8-block --port 8000 --seed 0 \
  --dataset-name hf --dataset-path lmarena-ai/VisionArena-Chat --hf-split train \
  --hf-output-len 8 --num-prompts 1000 --max-concurrency 1

# Video. For 4 images: 4 items per request, limit {"image": 4, "video": 0}, 200 prompts, concurrency 16,
# bucket config "{(768, 1024, 1): 0.4, (434, 600, 1): 0.3, (512, 512, 1): 0.3}"
vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --model RedHatAI/Muse-Glimmer-30B-FP8-block --port 8000 --seed 0 \
  --dataset-name random-mm --random-input-len 64 --random-output-len 64 \
  --random-mm-base-items-per-request 1 --random-mm-limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 0, "video": 1}' \
  --random-mm-bucket-config "{(720, 1280, 32): 1.0}" --num-prompts 30 --max-concurrency 1

# Encoder forward
vllm bench mm-processor --model RedHatAI/Muse-Glimmer-30B-FP8-block --max-model-len 16384 --seed 0 \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 4, "video": 1}' \
  --dataset-name random-mm --random-input-len 64 --random-mm-base-items-per-request 1 \
  --random-mm-limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 0, "video": 1}' \
  --random-mm-bucket-config "{(720, 1280, 32): 1.0}" --num-prompts 30
```

The encoder comparison uses a standalone script that isn't part of this PR. I can share it.

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** `_get_sparse_permutation` built the 32×32 window layout on the GPU, then did a boolean-mask select and a `.tolist()`: two syncs per image or frame group. NaViT's `_get_sparse_attention_perm` has the same mask select, plus a `.tolist()` per call and a blocking `torch.tensor(list, device=cuda)` in `_seqlens_to_cu_seqlens`. All of this depends only on the patch grid, which is already on the CPU.

**Change.** Layouts are computed in numpy with the same operations and copied with `async_tensor_h2d`. In Glimmer, layouts are built once per distinct grid. `ln_pre`, RoPE, the window permutation, `ln_post` and the pixel shuffle then run once over the whole call.

**Tradeoffs.**
- The patch projection stays one matmul per group. A single matmul over the call changed output bits on 48 of 126 calls on L4 but none on H100, so a bit-exact test on CI hardware might not catch it. `test_glimmer_vision_encoder_projects_patches_per_group` pins the call count instead.
- The position embedding is still interpolated per distinct grid on the GPU, which keeps its temporary no larger than on main.

**Limits.**
- No config, flag or API change.
- The Muse Spark checkpoint is gated, so NaViT is validated with a standalone 12-layer encoder (bit-identical, no syncs), not the full model.
- CI covers the tests above. Real-weight bit-identity and the benchmarks were run outside CI.

**Related PRs.** #59470 and #61448 also touch `muse_glimmer.py`, but only the language model and RMSNorm. I found no open PR addressing these syncs.

---

- [] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,313 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+from functools import partial
+
+import numpy as np
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+from PIL import Image
+from transformers import MuseGlimmerConfig
+
+import vllm.utils.gpu_sync_debug as gpu_sync_debug
+from vllm.model_executor.models.muse_glimmer import MuseGlimmerVisionEncoder
+from vllm.models.muse_spark.common.vision import (
+    NaViT,
+    _get_sparse_attention_perm,
+    _seqlens_to_cu_seqlens,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.sampling_params import SamplingParams
+from vllm.transformers_utils.configs.muse_spark import MuseSparkVisionConfig
+from vllm.utils.torch_utils import set_default_torch_dtype
+
+from ..registry import HF_EXAMPLE_MODELS
+from ..utils import dummy_hf_overrides
+
+GRIDS = [(2, 2), (16, 16), (32, 32), (34, 34), (64, 64), (74, 74), (22, 286), (96, 170)]
+
+
+def _block_major_order(grid_height: int, grid_width: int, block: int) -> np.ndarray:
+    rows, cols = np.divmod(np.arange(grid_height * grid_width), grid_width)
+    return np.lexsort((cols % block, rows % block, cols // block, rows // block))
+
+
+def _window_lengths(grid_height: int, grid_width: int) -> list[int]:
+    return [
+        min(32, grid_height - row) * min(32, grid_width - col)
+        for row in range(0, grid_height, 32)
+        for col in range(0, grid_width, 32)
+    ]
+
+
+def _check_without_gpu_sync(monkeypatch, fn, *args):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(gpu_sync_debug, "_SYNC_CHECK_MODE", "error")
+    monkeypatch.setattr(gpu_sync_debug, "_sync_check_enabled", False)
+    gpu_sync_debug.enable_gpu_sync_check()
+    return gpu_sync_debug.with_gpu_sync_check(fn)(*args)
+
+
+def _tiny_glimmer_encoder(
+    layer_types: list[str], dtype: torch.dtype, pos_emb_size: int = 4
+) -> MuseGlimmerVisionEncoder:
+    config = MuseGlimmerConfig(
+        vision_config=dict(
+            hidden_size=64,
+            intermediate_size=128,
+            num_attention_heads=4,
+            num_hidden_layers=len(layer_types),
+            layer_types=layer_types,
+            pos_emb_height=pos_emb_size,
+            pos_emb_width=pos_emb_size,
+        ),
+        out_hidden_size=256,
+    )
+    with torch.device("cuda"), set_default_torch_dtype(dtype):
+        encoder = MuseGlimmerVisionEncoder(config)
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        for param in encoder.parameters():
+            param.normal_(std=0.1)
+    return encoder
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def glimmer_layout_encoder(default_vllm_config, dist_init) -> MuseGlimmerVisionEncoder:
+    return _tiny_glimmer_encoder(["window_attention"], torch.float32, pos_emb_size=32)
+
+
+def _pixel_values(grid_thw: torch.Tensor, encoder: MuseGlimmerVisionEncoder):
+    return torch.randn(
+        int(grid_thw.prod(-1).sum()),
+        encoder.conv1_linear.in_features,
+        device="cuda",
+        dtype=encoder.conv1_linear.weight.dtype,
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.core_model
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not current_platform.is_cuda(), reason="Requires CUDA")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(("grid_height", "grid_width"), GRIDS)
+def test_glimmer_sparse_permutation_orders_tokens_by_window(
+    glimmer_layout_encoder: MuseGlimmerVisionEncoder, grid_height: int, grid_width: int
+) -> None:
+    permutation, seq_lens = glimmer_layout_encoder._get_sparse_permutation(
+        grid_height,
+        grid_width,
+    )
+
+    np.testing.assert_array_equal(
+        permutation, _block_major_order(grid_height, grid_width, block=32)
+    )
+    assert seq_lens == _window_lengths(grid_height, grid_width)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.core_model
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not current_platform.is_cuda(), reason="Requires CUDA")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(("grid_height", "grid_width"), GRIDS + [(128, 128)])
+def test_glimmer_pos_emb_layout_is_bilinear_interpolation(
+    glimmer_layout_encoder: MuseGlimmerVisionEncoder, grid_height: int, grid_width: int
+) -> None:
+    table = torch.randn(32, 32, 8, dtype=torch.float64)
+
+    indices, weights = glimmer_layout_encoder._get_pos_emb_layout(
+        grid_height,
+        grid_width,
+    )
+    actual = (
+        table.reshape(32 * 32, 8)[torch.from_numpy(indices)]
+        * torch.from_numpy(weights).double()[..., None]
+    ).sum(0)
+
+    y = (torch.arange(grid_height, dtype=torch.float64) + 0.5) / grid_height * 2 - 1
+    x = (torch.arange(grid_width, dtype=torch.float64) + 0.5) / grid_width * 2 - 1
+    grid = torch.stack(torch.meshgrid(x, y, indexing="xy"), dim=-1)[None]
+    expected = F.grid_sample(
+        table.permute(2, 0, 1)[None], grid, mode="bilinear", align_corners=False
+    )[0].reshape(8, -1)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected.T, rtol=0, atol=5e-5)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.core_model
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not current_platform.is_cuda(), reason="Requires CUDA")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(("grid_height", "grid_width"), [(2, 2), (6, 10), (74, 74)])
+def test_glimmer_pixel_shuffle_order_groups_merge_blocks(
+    glimmer_layout_encoder: MuseGlimmerVisionEncoder, grid_height: int, grid_width: int
+) -> None:
+    order = glimmer_layout_encoder._get_pixel_shuffle_order(
+        grid_height,
+        grid_width,
+    )
+
+    np.testing.assert_array_equal(
+        order, _block_major_order(grid_height, grid_width, block=2)
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.cpu_test
+@pytest.mark.core_model
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(("grid_height", "grid_width"), GRIDS)
+def test_navit_sparse_permutation_orders_tokens_by_window(
+    grid_height: int, grid_width: int
+) -> None:
+    offset = 7
+
+    permutation, seq_lens, next_offset = _get_sparse_attention_perm(
+        offset, grid_height, grid_width, 32, 32
+    )
+
+    np.testing.assert_array_equal(
+        permutation, offset + _block_major_order(grid_height, grid_width, block=32)
+    )
+    assert seq_lens.tolist() == _window_lengths(grid_height, grid_width)
+    assert next_offset == offset + grid_height * grid_width
+
+
+@pytest.mark.cpu_test
+@pytest.mark.core_model
+def test_navit_cu_seqlens() -> None:
+    cu_seqlens, max_seqlen = _seqlens_to_cu_seqlens([3, 1, 4], torch.device("cpu"))
+
+    assert cu_seqlens.dtype == torch.int32
+    assert cu_seqlens.tolist() == [0, 3, 4, 8]
+    assert max_seqlen.device.type == "cpu" and max_seqlen.item() == 4
+
+
+@pytest.mark.core_model
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not current_platform.is_cuda(), reason="Requires CUDA")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "layer_types",
+    [["window_attention", "full_attention"], ["full_attention", "full_attention"]],
+)
+def test_glimmer_vision_encoder_is_batch_invariant(
+    default_vllm_config, dist_init, layer_types: list[str]
+) -> None:
